title: Bully in the Alley
description: A pulling shanty as John Short of Watchet sang it to Cecil Sharp, for 2 to 4 singers: the soprano is the shantyman and sings each call alone, and everyone answers "Way ay bully in the alley" in harmony, landing together on "Way" and "bully", where Sharp marks the pulls. The refrain comes first, then three verses.

credits.words: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914)
credits.tune: traditional sea shanty (as sung by John Short, Watchet; printed 1914)

licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella on the harmony of Cecil Sharp's piano accompaniment (public domain: printed 1914, Sharp died 1924); the tune as printed, with breaths written in for beginners
licence.source: tune, words and harmony from Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys (London: Simpkin, Marshall, Hamilton, Kent & Co.; Schott & Co.; Taunton: Barnicott & Pearce, 1914), No. XXXV, "Bully in the Alley", pp. 40 to 41, with Sharp's note on p. 71 ("Sung by Mr. John Short, at Watchet. I have no variants of this nor do I know of any printed version of it."), in G major as printed and written here in G; the refrain and verse 1 as printed, verses 2 and 3 from the two lines Sharp prints after the tune ("Have you seen our Sally?", "She's the girl in the alley."), each in place of the verse's first solo line; pulls on Sharp's arrow-heads (his note on p. 32: "In this and the following chanteys arrow-heads are placed immediately over the notes upon which the pulls are made"). Read from the scan at archive.org/details/englishfolkchant00shar; in the refrain's first chorus, "al-ley," is sung an eighth earlier than printed (at beat 14.5), to give the shantyman a breath before "So"
